turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Alright, I weighed him just now. Seven point six pounds, heart rate a hundred and forty-two. He stayed pretty calm.
[SEG0002] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Thank you. That was very smooth, he usually objects to the scale.
[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): How was the drive? I was stuck past the mall forever, rain coming sideways, and my defroster is basically decorative.
[SEG0004] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Quite slow, I'm afraid. We sat at the river bridge nearly twenty minutes with the windshield completely fogged. I apologize if that put us behind.
[SEG0005] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): My husband argued for the back roads, and I overruled him, which was foolish. He is home with the dog, who has taken up residence in the laundry basket.
[SEG0006] person_3 (DOCTOR): Ha, the laundry basket always wins. I'm Dr. Ellison, by the way. This rain is meant to sit all weekend, just gray and heavy.
[SEG0007] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Yes. My mother will not stop texting about her tomato plants drowning. I told her the tomatoes can wait.
[SEG0008] person_3 (DOCTOR): They can. So, what brought you in with him today?
[SEG0009] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): His skin has gone yellow. That is why we came.
[SEG0010] person_4 (PATIENT): Mm.
[SEG0011] person_3 (DOCTOR): Yellow. When did you first notice it?
[SEG0012] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Umm. I cannot really date it. It crept up on us, maybe a few days, but I am not certain.
[SEG0013] person_3 (DOCTOR): That's alright. A lot of this age is hard to date. How have the feeds been?

[SEG0014] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He takes the breast, and we give formula too. I nearly said every three hours, well, actually it is every four. The nursery doctor also said he has eczema on his cheeks.
[SEG0015] person_3 (DOCTOR): Eczema, okay, noted. Is he hard to wake for a feed?
[SEG0016] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No. He wakes quite reliably on his own.
[SEG0017] person_4 (PATIENT): Ah.
[SEG0018] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any fever?
[SEG0019] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No.
[SEG0020] person_3 (DOCTOR): Vomiting?
[SEG0021] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Not really.
[SEG0022] person_3 (DOCTOR): And diarrhea?
[SEG0023] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Never.
[SEG0024] person_3 (DOCTOR): With the eczema, does the skin weep or ooze?
[SEG0025] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Not that either.
[SEG0026] person_3 (DOCTOR): Does he seem itchy? Scratching at the cheeks?
[SEG0027] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No... well, sometimes he rubs his cheek against my shoulder.
[SEG0028] person_3 (DOCTOR): Sometimes, then. Any cough, or breathing that seems too fast?
[SEG0029] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No. Not the cough, and not the fast breathing either.
[SEG0030] person_3 (DOCTOR): Does his belly hurt him, do you think?
[SEG0031] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No, he is not in pain.
[SEG0032] person_3 (DOCTOR): Looking at digestion more broadly, anything else with his belly that worries you?
[SEG0033] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No. Nothing else there.
[SEG0034] person_3 (DOCTOR): Have the wet diapers dropped off?
[SEG0035] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No.

[SEG0036] person_1 (NURSE): Sorry to butt in. My sister's boy was yellow last spring, and she still texts me at odd hours about those blue lights. He's chubby now, so, uh, that's her story, not advice.
[SEG0037] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Of course. Thank you, that is kind to mention.
[SEG0038] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any medicines at home?
[SEG0039] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Yes, Doctor. We give d-vysol, vitamin d drops, four hundred units once a day by mouth. Err, I think we missed yesterday. The bottle stayed in the other bag.
[SEG0040] person_3 (DOCTOR): Four hundred units a day, and yesterday is a maybe. Any allergies?
[SEG0041] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No. None.
[SEG0042] person_3 (DOCTOR): Let me look him over. You can keep a hand on him.
[SEG0043] person_3 (DOCTOR): The eyes are yellow, and the color comes down across his chest and belly. Belly is soft, and I don't feel an enlarged liver.
[SEG0044] person_3 (DOCTOR): The soft spot is flat. He seems comfortable enough.
[SEG0045] person_4 (PATIENT): Uh.

[SEG0046] person_3 (DOCTOR): That yellow is bilirubin. At ten days the liver is still maturing, so pigment from old red cells builds up and stains the skin. Breast milk can slow the clearing a little. I think this is ordinary newborn jaundice.
[SEG0047] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I understand. I appreciate you explaining it plainly.
[SEG0048] person_3 (DOCTOR): I'd like a blood test for bilirubin today, before you leave. The lab down the hall can draw it.
[SEG0049] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Yes. Today is quite alright with us.
[SEG0050] person_3 (DOCTOR): If the level is high, we might start phototherapy. I won't decide that until we see the number.
[SEG0051] person_3 (DOCTOR): Either way, I want to see him back in three days. We'll call you this afternoon with the result.
[SEG0052] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): We will be by the phone. Should feeding change at all?

[SEG0053] person_3 (DOCTOR): Keep the breast milk and the formula, and try not to go much past four hours. Wake him if you have to. Call or come sooner if he's hard to wake, if the yellow reaches his legs, or if the wet diapers thin out.

spec.situation: Parents with a ten-day-old baby, yellow skin and feeding every four hours; weight read by the nurse; breast milk plus formula; blood test for bilirubin planned today.

traps.happens: The patient denies some symptoms (said as 'no', 'not really', 'never'), has a chronic condition named earlier (for example asthma or hypertension) and later the doctor asks about another symptom of it, and one answer is a double negative or a correction ('not that either', 'no... well, sometimes').
traps.label_rule: Denials go in negative_findings with the exact thing denied, never in symptoms. NEVER write a negative about a condition the patient has said they have. A corrected answer keeps only the final version. A negative is never a symptom, and 'not painful' is the finding 'pain' absent, not a symptom called 'painless'.

traps.happens: The doctor (or nurse) explains a mechanism or a diagnosis in the patient's body ('the voice box is irritated by reflux', 'diabetes dulls the nerves in the feet', 'the swelling is your body fighting infection'). A nurse or caregiver also mentions a fact about THEIR OWN life (their sister, their child, their own illness).
traps.label_rule: Explanations by the doctor are NEVER symptoms, history or social history of the patient; they may only appear as clinical_assessment or counselling if the doctor stated them as such. A nurse's or caregiver's own life facts are not recorded as the patient's. Each symptom's reported_by is the person who really described it.

features: tangent_small_talk: a long tangent or small talk (traffic, cricket, the weather, a grandchild) that holds NO clinical content; nothing from it is extracted.

spoken_numbers: doses, vitals and durations are spoken as words or sloppy speech ('a hundred and two point five', 'one-forty over ninety', 'five-ish years', 'twenty milligram'); the label writes them normally (102.5, 140/90, 20 mg) and does not turn vague ones into exact ones.
